column2: *** THE 1921 ENGLAND AND WALES CENSUS *** - every Taylor sibling and their children
column3: *** EXCLUSIVE TO FINDMYPAST. *** It is not on FamilySearch at any price, and the 1931 returns were destroyed by fire, so 1921 is the LAST census until the 1939 Register
column4: Where all ten siblings had landed; the Dalling, Burton, Bell, Sweet and Wood households complete; and whether KATHLEEN GEORGINA, single at 41 in 1911, was still single at 51.

column2: *** OUTBOUND PASSENGER LISTS (BT27), 1890-1920 *** - for MARY SEPTIMA TAYLOR, and for PABLO ARMANDO
column3: Findmypast holds BT27 outbound. This is the single biggest open question on the Taylor page
column4: *** THE EIGHT-YEAR HOLE. *** How a Devon pupil-teacher of sixteen in 1901 reached Cape Town and bore a son there in November 1905. A departure record would name the ship, the date and the party she travelled with.

column3: Findmypast holds it; it is the substitute for the lost 1931 census
column4: Addresses, occupations and MARRIED SURNAMES for the five sisters who lived into the 1950s-70s - Irene to 1969, Agnes to 1974, Isabella to 1953, Margaret after 1953, Lucy to 1957.

column2: *** DEVON PARISH REGISTER IMAGES *** behind the five marriages found today
column3: Today's five husbands came from an INDEX. This archive's own rule is never to rest on an index
column4: The acts themselves: fathers' names and occupations for Dalling, Burton, Bell, Sweet and Wood - a whole generation of in-laws currently unknown.

column4: Mary Septima's teaching career (the Western Times already gave her 1901 exam result); marriage and death notices; and any Lerena mention in the British press.

column1: # *** WHAT NOT TO SPEND THE LAST DAY ON. *** Anything FamilySearch also holds: GRO index entries,
# baptisms already read, Uruguayan and Argentine records. Findmypast adds nothing there, and those
# sources will still be free next week.
# *** AND A DISCIPLINE NOTE FOR A RUSHED HARVEST. *** The temptation under a deadline is to screenshot
# and sort later. *** Do not. *** This archive's whole method is that a record is READ, TIERED and
# CITED at the moment it is opened. A folder of unread images is not evidence, and in a fortnight
# nobody will remember which was which. Capture the citation - collection, piece, folio, schedule -
